He was also a stranger in Mitzrayim. He was few in number. He then became a large nation. You O Hashem took us out of slavery and gave us a good land. Let the one who disputes not argue, “How could Yaakov be called an Arami?” Look, we find the same with Yitra the Yishmeeli who, as Scripture clearly states, was a Yisraeli.

Few in number. The word mete (men of) is in the construct, for it is not found in the singular. The word metim is a plural. Rabbi Yonah the grammarian explained it very well under the entry mem, tav, heh.
Our affliction. In lacking wealth.
Our toil. In building.
Our oppression. As in [And the taskmasters] were urgent, saying: Fulfill your work (Shemot 5:13). 11.
[Thou, and the Levi, and the stranger.] This means you are obligated to cheer them up with the fruit of your land.
Of tithing. La-ser (of tithing) is a hifil. It has no neighbor.
Which is the year of tithing. The reference is to the poor tithe.
Unto the Levi, to the stranger, to the fatherless. To any one of them that you wish.
I have put away the hallowed things. The reference is to the tithe. I have also not deposited it. On the contrary, I have handed it over to the one I am obligated to give it to.
I have not transgressed. Deliberately.
Neither have I forgotten them. I did not forget to take the tithes from my house. Or its meaning is, I did not forget to give the two tithes.

I have not eaten thereof in my mourning. The word oni (my mourning) is similar to the word oni (sorrow) in ben-oni (the son of my sorrow) (Bereshit 35:18) and onim (mourners) in bread of mourners (Hoshea 9:4). I alluded to its meaning in Hebrew. The meaning of oni is, my mourning. If I was in mourning then I did not eat of it before setting aside the tithe.
Neither have I put away thereof. This means neither did I destroy any of that which was holy.
Being unclean. Be-tame (being unclean) means for something unclean.

For the dead. For the need of the dead. Others say the reference is to idol worship. These things are enumerated because it is prohibited to use the grain for any purpose before giving of the tithe which is holy. If he gives from the remainder he is acting disrespectfully. This is certainly so if he exchanges it for something unclean. As I kept myself and I kept the grain, that is, I removed that which is holy from my house, so may our Elokim watch over our country. This is the meaning of and the land (v. 15).
[A land flowing with milk and honey.] It means a land that will always flow with milk and honey.
This day. These are the words of Moshe.
Thou shalt therefore observe. In your heart.
And do them. In the land.

Thou hast avouched. He’emarta (avouched) means exalted. It is close in meaning to amir (uppermost bough) in In the top of the uppermost bough (Is. 17:6). Rabbi Yehudah Ha-Levi, who rests in Eden, says that the word is related to va-yomer (said). Its meaning is, you were so righteous that the Lord said He is your Elokim. Elokim likewise acted very righteously towards you that you said that you would be His own treasure. He explained well. Now the word he’emarta is a hifil.
And to make thee high. This is the reward for extolling God.
And Moshe…commanded. By the dictate of Hashem.
And the elders of Yisrael. He said this to lighten his load. There are many such instances. I have previously noted them.

Keep all the commandments. Namely, that thou shalt set thee up great stones to contain the entire Torah. The Gaon, of blessed memory, said that the commandments were listed upon the stones, as in the Halakhot Gedolot. They were listed in a manner similar to the azharot. He explained well.
[With plaster] Plaster was employed so that it would last.

That thou mayest. For Hashem will aid you if you begin to observe His commandments. This first precept upon entering the Land of Yisrael, namely, the command to build a new altar, was to give thanks to Hashem for their starting to inherit the land.
Very plainly. The reference is to the writing.
And Moshe and the priests the Leviyim. This is in keeping with Scripture’s statement, and the elders of Yisrael (v. 1). Moshe was the main one.
Keep silence. The meaning of the word hasket (keep silence) can only be known from its context, for it has no neighbor.
This day thou art become a people. For God will make a covenant with you.
Thou shalt therefore hearken. Today, to His voice.
And do his commandments. In the future.

Scripture mentions the priests and the Leviyim (v. 9), for they are the ones who said, Cursed be the man (v. 15). The children of the main wives stood over the blessings, while the children of the handmaids stood over the curse. Now if the latter lacked two, the sons of Leah were numerous, and her oldest and youngest were taken.

And the Leviyim shall speak. Ve-anu (shall speak) is similar to ve-anita (and thou shalt speak) in And thou shalt speak and say (Devarim 26:5). Our rabbis, of blessed memory, said that the meaning of to bless is to say, blessed is the man who does not make a graven or molten image, and similarly all of them. However, according to the plain meaning of the text, the blessing refers to Blessed shalt thou be in the city (Devarim 28:3). The curse is the reverse of this. Proof of this is found in the Book of Yehoshua.

Scripture mentions these eleven sins because an individual can commit them in secret. And setteth it up in secret (v. 15) is proof, for if one commits this crime in the open he is put to death. He that smiteth his neighbor in secret (v. 24) is similar. Scripture begins with the most important, namely, that which concerns a person and his creator. It then speaks of a person and his parents, for who knows if he dishonors them.
Dishonoreth. The word makleh (dishonoreth) means to dishonor. It is a transitive verb.
Cursed be he that removeth his neighbor’s landmark. For it is done in secret. [MAKETH THE BLIND TO GO ASTRAY.] Likewise it is not possible for the blind person to identify the one who led him astray.

Cursed be he that perverteth the justice due to the stranger, fatherless. For they have no one to help them. Look, this too is done in secret. Scripture mentions the stranger as well as the orphan and the widow because if the judge perverts the justice due others, they will accuse and publicize him. The stranger, the orphan, and the widow are powerless. Sleeping with one’s father’s wife, with a sister, or with a mother-in-law is an act that is committed in secret, for one is not suspected when he is alone with any one of them. It is not so with other sins.

Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast. Male or female, for neither have a mouth with which to cry out and protest. Thus, a female animal is like a male animal; therefore Scripture does not mention the male.
He that taketh a bribe. According to many the reference is to the judge. According to my opinion the reference is to a false witness.

That confirmeth not. Some say that the reference is to the entire Torah. Others say that it refers to the specifically mentioned sins. However, what they say is meaningless, for Scripture says, to do them. However, it appears to me that Scripture cursed the violators of the precepts which are mentioned. It also cursed the one who secretly does not observe the positive commandments. Scripture therefore reads, to do them.
On high above all the nations of the earth. This is a general blessing. It states that there will be no nation in the world like you.
[And…shall come.] The meaning of And…shall come is that they shall come by themselves.
And overtake thee. Even though you do not pursue them. It means that you will not tire yourself.
In the city. This is a blessing regarding an increase in merchandise.
In the field. In seeding and planting.
The fruit of thy body. Sons. The word beten (body) is a euphemism.
The increase of…and the young. I have previously explained the meaning of these two phrases.
Thy basket. The place of bread. Thy basket precedes and thy kneading trough but should come after it. On the other hand, thy basket may refer to the place where the flour is placed.

When thou goest out. To celebrate festivals, to engage in business, and to take spoil, or in all your daily comings and goings. Its meaning is, you shall be successful in all that you do. The reverse is written [in the curses].

[That rise up against thee.] Since Scripture earlier stated that God will set Yisrael on high above the nations (v. 1), it now goes on to say that should the nations revolt against Yisrael [the Lord will cause thine enemies] that rise up against thee [to be smitten before thee].
And…seven. This means many. The number seven is employed because of the continuous cycle of seven days of the week. It has a set number of days because is contingent on the bodies which are on high.
In thy barns. Ba-asamekha (in thy bams) is in your storehouses. Its meaning is determined by its context.
For a holy people. Holy by observing God’s commandments.
The meaning of yekimekha is, will establish thee.
Shalt keep. In your heart.
And walk. Practice.
And…will make thee overabundant. The meaning of and will make thee overabundant is, if evil comes to the world, if hunger or blight comes, you will be set aside for good.

His…treasure. Which is potentially ready in heaven to go out. Compare, the treasuries of the snow (Iyov 38:22). Scripture speaks of rain after stating will make thee overabundant, for the withholding of rain is the cause of famine.
And thou shalt lend unto many nations. For they shall suffer famine. However, no time shall come where you shall borrow. The sum of the matter is, you will always be on top.

If thou shalt hearken. In your heart to observe and to do. The sum of the matter is, do not turn aside from Hashem to serve idols, for the root of all sins is to deny Hashem. The reverse of the aforementioned is to affirm that Hashem is one and to hearken and to observe, for the most important aspect of hearkening is observing.
Cursing. Diminution.
Discomfiture. A state wherein one can not finish what he has started.
Rebuke. A state in which one cannot enjoy what he has worked for, but is concerned for it after he has toiled.
Consumption. Some say that shachefet (consumption) refers to various types of illnesses.

With fever. Each day. Kaddachat (fever) is related to kadechah (kindled) in For a fire is kindled (Devarim 32:22). The words mehumah (discomfiture), migeret (rebuke), shachefet (consumption), kaddachat (fever) and dalleket (inflammation) are adjectives.
Dalleket refers to a fever which comes every third or fourth day.
And with fiery heat. The word charchur (fiery heat) is related to the word charah (bum) in and the bottom thereof may burn (Yechezkel 24:11).
And with drought. The word cherev (drought) is related to the word chorev (dry).
And with blasting. Shiddafon (blasting) means bloating. Compare, shedufot kadim (blasted with the east wind) (Bereshit 41:23). Others say the reverse is true. Its meaning is then thin.

And with mildew. Yerakon (mildew) is to be rendered according to its meaning in Arabic. Some say that these refer to diseases of the seed. U-vashiddafon (blasting) is similar to shidufot (blasted) in blasted with the east wind (Bereshit 41:23). I have smitten you with blasting (shiddafon) and mildew (Amos 4:9) is proof. Therefore Scripture afterwards reads, and thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass. We find the same in the Torah portion If Ye Walk in My Statutes (Vayikra 26:3).
Brass. Like brass. The same applies to iron.
Powder and dust. Because of the great dryness and the power of the winds.
Until thou be destroyed. Hishamedakh (thou be destroyed) is irregular. Compare, hibbare’akh (in the day that thou wast created) (Yechezkel 28:15).
A horror. Some of the letters of za’avah (horror) are reversed. Compare, keves (lamb) and kesev (lamb).
And there shall be none to frighten them away. To frighten away the birds and beasts.
[The boil of Mitzrayim.] Those who remain will be struck with the boil of Mitzrayim.

And with the emerods. They appear in the hidden places. Scripture therefore reads u-vafolim (and with the emerods). The latter is related to the world ofel (hill) in And when he came to the hill (Melachim II 5:24).
And with the scab. The same is true in Arabic.

And with the itch. Some say that he will need a potsherd as Iyov did. This is so even though the word cheres (itch) is spelled with a samekh. Others say u-ve-chares (and with the itch) means: and with a blow from the sun. However, the correct interpretation is that cheres (itch) refers to the name of a disease like the ones mentioned previously. The word has no neighbor.
Madness…] Madness, blindness, and astonishment are afflictions of the heart.
And thou shalt grope. In blindness.
Prosperous. Tatzli’ach (prosperous) is a transitive verb.
Oppressed and robbed. By the enemy, and there shall be none to save thee. Scripture commences to explain in what manner Yisrael shall be oppressed.
Shall lie with her. Yishgalennah (lie with her) is a euphemism for sexual intercourse. The same applies to the word shegal (the queen) (Tehillim 45:10). It refers to a woman prepared for bed.
Use the fruit therefof. Techallennu (use the fruit thereof) is related to the word chalil (flute).

And fail with longing. The word kalot (fail with longing) is similar to the word kaletah (pineth) in My soul yearneth, yea, even pineth (Tehillim 84:3) and to va-tekhal (failed with longing) in va-tekhal david (and caused David to fail with longing) (Shmuel II 13:39). The latter is not lacking the word “soul” as the one lacking in knowledge says, for the word vatekhal is transitive. The subject is omitted, as it is in “whom she bore” (Bamidbar 26:59).
And crushed. Powerfully so.
Mad. This explains with madness (v. 28.). He will see his body covered with boils (v. 35).
In the knees, and in the legs. For when the boils are upon the knees and the legs, [it is hard to remove them].
Whereof thou canst not be healed. Because they are on the surface of the body.
And there shalt thou serve. And it shall not avail you but you shall become an astonishment. That is, all who see you shall be astonished.
A proverb. In the ear.
And a byword. In the mouth. Sheninah (byword) is related to the word ve-shinnantam (and thou shalt teach them diligently) (Devarim 6:7).
Shall lead thee. Because of your sins. However, before this, a year of hunger shall come upon you when you are still in your land.
Shall consume them. Yachselennu (shall consume them) means shall destroy them. Yachselennu comes from chasil, which is the name of a type of grasshopper.
Plant. You shall toil in planting and in the vineyards.
But thou shalt neither drink of the wine. At the time of the harvest.
Nor gather the grapes. Te’egor (gather the grapes) means you will gather. It is a verb. Te’egor is similar to agerah (gathereth) in And gathereth her food in the harvest (Mishlei 6:8).
But thou shalt not annoint thyself with the oil. As is the practice. Compare, neither did I anoint myself at all (Daniel 10:3). This is the reverse of And let thy head lack no oil (Kohelet 9:8).
Shall drop off. Yishal (drop off) is a nifal.
Shall…possess. Yeyaresh (shall possess) is a pi’el. Yeyaresh is similar to le-horish (to drive out) in to drive out nations (Bamidbar 4:38).
The locust. Tzelatzal (locust) is a quadriliteral. It has no neighbor. Its meaning is according to its place.
Higher and higher. The word is repeated to indicate a height over which no one else towers. On the other hand it may indicate permanency. Lower and lower is similar. Its meaning is very low.
He shall be the head. As in And the borrower is servant to the lender (Mishlei 22:7).

For a sign. From Hashem, so that you remember that you rebelled against Him. It will not only be a sign in you but also in your offspring, as in Our fathers have sinned, and are not (Eichah 5:7). I have previously explained this.
By reason of the abundance of all things. Which you desired, or all your needs.
Swoopeth down. Yideh (swoopeth down) means flies. Compare, va-yede (he did swoop down) in Yea, He did swoop down upon the wings of the wind (Tehillim 18:11).
And thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body. During the siege.
Shall straiten thee. Each one of your enemies. Or the word oyevekha is so vocalized because it comes at the end of a verse.
Whom he hath remaining. This refers to the enemy. Or it means which he will leave over by hiding them. All of this will he due to the siege.
In all thy gates. In any place.
And against her afterbirth. Shilyah (afterbirth) refers to the place where the child dwells while in the mother’s belly.
From between her feet. This is a euphemism. Compare, and he had neither dressed his feet (Shmuel II 19:25).
Thy plagues. Makkotekha (thy plagues) is a compound of a singular and the plural. Compare, the word edoti (my testimony) in And My testimony that I shall teach them (Tehillim 132:12).
The meaning of ve-hifla (will make wonderful) is, it will be an extraordinary thing, for nothing like it was ever seen or heard of.
Of long continuance. They will not be removed.

Will Hashem bring upon. Yalem (will bring) is related to the word he’elah (brought up) (Yirmiyahu 16:15) even though it is vocalized with a sheva. Others say that yalem means will bring. It is an Aramaic word.
As the Lord rejoiced. You should not think that this will harm God or that God will mourn. Its meaning is similar to If thou he righteous, what givest thou to him (Iyov 35:7).
And ye shall be plucked. Ve-nissachtem (and ye shall be plucked) is a nifal. It is lacking a nun. It is related to the word yissach (will pluck) in Hashem will pluck up (Mishlei 15:25).
Shall hang. The word telu’im (shall hang) has an alef in place of the stem heh.

And…ye shall sell yourselves. Ve-hitmakkartem (and ye shall sell yourselves) does not mean and you will be sold. It means you, both men and women, will seek to sell yourselves and no man shall buy you. Observe, this covenant was made by the command of Hashem in the plains of Moav.
And Moshe called unto all Yisrael. To establish a covenant. Scripture therefore reads afterwards, Ye are standing this day (v. 9).

The reason Scripture reads Ye have seen and then And I have led (v. 4) and then And Og…came out (v. 6) is that some of Bnei Yisrael saw the signs that Hashem showed in Mitzrayim, and they and those who came after them saw the miracle of the manna, for they ate no food aside from the manna. And these sons saw that Hashem helped them and they smote two kings (v. 6).
[But Hashem hath not given you a heart to know.] Scripture reads a heart to know because they tested Hashem ten times and did not make mention of the signs which they witnessed.
Scripture reads given because God is the first cause. Furthermore, they saw that they had no need for bread or wine.
[Are not waxen old.] I have previously explained this. Sichon and Og were recently defeated. You are therefore obligated to keep the covenant.
That ye may…prosper. Taskilu means prosper. It is a hifil as the word ta’asun (all that ye do) proves. Compare, maskil (great success) in And David had great success in all his ways (Shmuel I 18:14).
Ye are standing this day. Around the ark.

Your heads. Roshekhem (your heads) is similar to haohelah (the tent) in into the tent Sarah his mother (Bereshit 24:67) and even the prophecy, Odad the prophet (Divrei Hayamim II 15:8). Roshekhem shivtekhem (your heads, your tribes) is to be interpreted as your heads, who are the heads of your tribes. Roshekhem (your heads) is like the word va-niram (we have shot at them) (Bamidbar 21:30). The word is to be so interpreted for the princes were closest to the ark. After them came the elders, followed by the officers, after whom came all the men of Yisrael, that is, the males, followed by the male little ones, after whom came the women, followed by the strangers.

That thou shouldest enter into the covenant. Le-ovrekha (that thou shouldest enter) is an infinitive. It is like va-ya’avru (and passed) in and passed between the parts thereof (Yirmiyahu 34:18). Observe, the word avar (passed) minus the bet has the opposite meaning.
Neither with you only. But with you and with those who come after you, namely, your sons and your sons’ sons.
[But with him that standeth here with us this day.] The nun of yeshno (that standth here) is superfluous.

And also with him that is not here with us. Ve’et asher ennnu (and also with him that is not) means with him that is not here with us but will come after us. It is not to be interpreted as those who say that the spirits of the coming generations were there.
For ye know. There are among you some who witnessed the abominations of Mitzrayim, namely, their gods. Additionally, all of you have seen the abominations of the nations.
Which ye passed. Among them, namely, the Edomim, Bnei Amon, the Moavim, and the Midyanim.
[A root that beareth gall and wormwood.] For gall injures the healthy. It is a disease that is infectious.
This curse. This curse refers to Cursed be the man that maketh a graven or molten image (Devarim 27:15).

That he bless himself in his heart. Rabbi Yehudah Ha-Levi, of blessed memory, says that he bless himself is to be taken according to its plain meaning. When he hears the curse he will bless himself in his heart and say I shall have peace. In other words, when he hears the ban he will say it will not fall on me but upon someone else.

That…be swept away. Rabbi Yehudah Ha-Levi, who rests in paradise, says that the word sefot (swept away) means to extirpate. Compare, tispeh [thou (wilt) sweep away] in Wilt Thou indeed sweep away (Bereshit 18:23). In other words, the one who blesses himself wants to nullify the words of the righteous, who are metaphorically called “the watered,” with the words of “the dry.” Look, the righteous are called watered. Compare, For he shall be like a tree planted by the streams of water (Yirmiyahu 17:8). The wicked are called dry. Compare, For he shall be like a tamarisk in the desert (Ibid., v. 6). The wicked person thinks that the blessing which he utters in his heart will also stop the curse. He explained well were it not that the word ravah (well watered) is an adjective. Our text should have read, ravi et ha-tzama (the well watered…with the dry). Rabbi Yonah the grammarian says that it means because the corrupt sees the righteous destroyed along with the wicked he therefore thinks evil in his heart. However, this is incorrect because Scripture reads, I shall have peace. In my opinion the word sefot (swept) means to add. Compare, sefot chattat (add sin) (Is. 30:1). The added sin is the wicked person’s statement, I shall have peace even though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart. I will live because of the righteousness of the righteous, for the pious are many and I am an individual sinner. Scripture therefore afterwards reads, Hashem will not be willing to pardon him but then… (v. 19). The meaning of the latter is he shall immediately be destroyed. This verse is also proof of my interpretation of and he shall be forgiven (Bamidbar 15:28). The meaning of sefot is that the well watered will add to the dry. Scripture compares the righteous to the well watered, as in And he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water (Tehillim 1:3). It compares the wicked to the dry. Compare, For he shall be like a tamarisk in the desert (Yirmiyahu 17: 6). The fact that Scripture at first reads, a root that beareth gall and wormwood (v. 17), is proof of this. It is in a dry place.

The anger of Hashem…shall be kindled. The fire of Hashem’s anger shall bum him to the point where the smoke will be visible. Observe, if the sinner be an individual he will die immediately, and if it is a family all the curse…shall lie upon him. This means that the curse shall lie upon the family until its name is eradicated. If the sinner be a tribe, Hashem shall separate him unto evil (v. 20). Similarly And I will offer it up for a burnt-offering (Jud. 11:31), as I have explained.
And the generation to come. Your children. Also the foreigners who see the plagues of the land.

Brimstone. A prayer to God that all the land should be burnt in brimstone and salt like the overthrow of the places that are mentioned. Some explain that even all the nations shall say (v. 23) repeats what was stated earlier because Scripture went off on a tangent, as is the style of the language. [24.] THEN MEN SHALL SAY. The earlier inhabitants.
[The Elokim of their fathers.] They forsook the Elokim that they and their fathers knew and they served gods whom they did not know.
And that he had not allotted unto them. I have previously explained this.
And the Lord rooted them out. Va-yitteshem (and rooted them out) is missing a nun. Compare li-netosh (to root out) (Yirmiyahu 1:10). The nun is swallowed by the dagesh, as is the rule.
[As is this day.] These are the words of the respondents.
The secret things. The reference is to one who serves idols in secret.

Belong unto Hashem our Elokim. Its meaning is that his punishment is in the hands of Elokim, and Hashem will exact punishment from him. However, if the sin was committed in public there is an obligation on us and our children to do in accordance with that which is written in the Torah. Others say that the secret and the revealed things belong to Elokim. It is incumbent upon us only to observe the words of the Torah. Now this interpretation has no head or foot. What reason is there to mention this here? Scripture states that if you return unto Hashem (Devarim 30:2), Elokim will turn thy captivity (Ibid., v. 3) even though you are outside of the land because it stated earlier, and cast them into another land (v. 27). According to Rabbi Yehudah the first grammarian, the meaning of ve-shav (then shall turn) (Devarim 30:3) means Elokim will give rest; that is, he will give rest to the captives and be merciful to them, and after this He will return and gather.
In the uttermost parts of heaven. With regard to the Land of Yisrael.

And Hashem thy Elokim will circumcise. For He is the first cause of all actions. After saying, you shall return unto Hashem and listen to His voice, Moshe says that unlike the circumcision of the flesh, which you are obligated to execute, Elokim will help you and will circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed.
[And the Lord thy God will make thee overabundant.] Scripture states ve-hotirekha (make thee overabundant) because God will place curses upon the enemies [of Yisrael]
As he rejoiced over thy fathers. Who inherited the land, for Scripture addresses those who were exiled from it.

Which are written in this book of the law. For the main part of all the commandments is there, although they need the explanation provided by tradition. They cannot be kept unless the heart is complete. Scripture therefore states, with all thy heart, for the commandment to keep means to keep with one’s heart.
Too hard. The word niflet (too hard) means concealed. Or its meaning is, wondrous, that is, something that will cause you to grow weary while trying to accomplish it.
It is not in heaven. This explains niflet (too hard) (v. 11).
Beyond the sea. This explains neither is it far off (v. 11). It is possible that the reference is to the great sea whose width a person cannot enter because of the darkness of the water.

In thy mouth, and in thy heart. For the heart is the core of the commandments. Some commandments require the uttering of statements which serve to reinforce the heart. Others consist of deeds so that a person will utter the required statements.
Life. Long life.
And good. Wealth, bodily health and honor.
Death and evil are the reverse of the above.
To love. This is most important.
To walk in his ways. You shall not modify the way He asked you to act and the precepts which He commanded you, even though you do not know why the statutes and ordinances were given.
Note, Then thou shalt live explains the term life (v. 15).
And multiply. This explains and good (v. 15), for it refers to material increase, that is, in children and in wealth.
But if thy heart turn away. For the heart is most important.
But shalt be drawn away. I have previously explained the meaning of ve-niddachta (but shall be drawn away).
That ye shall surely perish. This explains death and evil (v. 15), for they and their children and their wealth shall perish.
Ye shall not prolong your days. The reverse of Hashem thy Elokim shall bless thee in the land (v. 16).
Heaven and earth. For they endure. Similarly with regard to this stone shall be a witness against us (Yehoshua 24:27) and Hear, O ye mountains, Hashem’s controversy (Michah 6:2).
Life and death. The reference is to the blessing and the curse. Observe, it is incumbent upon you to choose life.
That thou mayest live. Physically or in memory. Scripture explains that life is to love.

For that is thy life. According to the commentaries this refers to the voice of Elokim. I believe that the reference is to Elokim, as the poet says, Hashem is my salvation; The Elokim of my mercy (Tehillim 59:11); My shield (Tehillim 18:3); and my sword.

And Moshe went. Moshe went to each tribe and tribe to inform them that he was about to die and that they should not fear. He strengthened them with his words to Yehoshua. Scripture therefore afterwards reads, and thou shalt cause them to inherit it (v. 7). I believe that he then blessed the tribes. This is so even though the blessings are recorded later.

Go out and come in. In war. Even if I did not die now, I would not have the ability to wage war. You have no need for any person to help you, for Hashem will destroy the nations. Yehoshua will do the same. What you saw with your eyes in the war of Sichon and Og is proof.
And ye shall do unto them. To break their pillars.
Be strong and of good courage. Now that you know that Hashem goes with you wherever you go to battle.
Be strong and of good courage. Moshe also said this to Yehoshua whom he appointed over them.
For thou shalt go with this people. The word et means with.
And delivered it unto the priests the sons of Levi. Who teach the Torah.
And unto all the elders of Yisrael. The Sanhedrin. Or its meaning is like And Moshe and the elders of Yisrael commanded (Devarim 27:1).
At the end of every seven years. At the beginning of the year.
That they may learn. The entire year. Similarly on the Sabbath.
And thy stranger. Perhaps he will convert to Judaism.
[That they may hear, and that they may learn.] When they hear they will ask. And he who is not wise and the children who are young will learn.
Thy days approach that thou must die. For there is a time set for each and everyone. I have previously explained this.
And Moshe…went. From the camp of Yisrael, for that is where he was. He then came to the camp where God’s presence rested.

And Hashem appeared in the tent. The specified tent. The meaning of our verse is that the pillar of cloud was at the door of the tent and Hashem was seen inside the tent. This is what the glory refers to. The statement that I may give him a charge (v. 14) refers to And he gave Yehoshua the son of Nun a charge (v. 23) by the command of Hashem, may He be blessed. Scripture therefore reads, which I swore unto them (Ibid.). After this came the passage Behold, thou art about to sleep with thy fathers (v. 16). There is no chronological order in the Torah. The passage And it came to pass, when Moshe had made an end of writing the words of this law (v. 24) is connected to And Moshe wrote this law (v. 9).
And this people will rise up. It is not possible for this to be connected to what precedes it, for what reason is there to say, and this people will rise up, and go astray.
The meaning of ve-zanah (and go astray) is, to leave God’s authority in one’s thought.

After the foreign gods of the land. We know that God is one. Change comes from the recepients. God does not change His works, for they are executed in wisdom. It is part of the service of God to harness one’s power to receive spiritual inspiration in accordance with the place. Scripture therefore reads, the manner of the God of the land (Melachim II 17:26). Yaakov therefore said, Put away the strange gods (Bereshit 35:2). The place is unlike other places with regard to engaging in sexual intercourse with women whom Scripture deems as being of close flesh. The intelligent will understand.

[Among them.] Be-kirbo (among them) refers to foreign. Scripture, as it were, states, and go astray after the gods of a foreign people, who are the gods of the land. However, it appears that be-kirbo refers to the word ha-aretz (of the land), for the word eretz is found in the masculine. Compare, And the land (ha-aretz) was not able to bear (nasa) them (Bereshit 13:6); the land [is] burnt up (netam aretz) (Is. 9:18).
And I will forsake them. All of them.
And they shall be. Each one of them shall be food for the enemy.

[And I will surely hide.] The meaning of And I will surely hide is, if they call Me, I will not answer. Scripture compares God to a person who does not see or know what is happening. It is the custom of Scripture to employ two verbs. Those who know grammar understand this.
In that they are turned. This, as I previously explained, is the great evil. There is no evil which tops it.
Now…write this. A commandment that Moshe, and all who know how to write, should write it.
And teach thou it. Explain to them the difficult meanings.
Put it in their mouths. That they should be able to recite it orally.
The words ve-lammedah (and teach thou it) and also simah (put it) are irregular, for grammatically the heh of ve-lammedah should have been vocalized with a kamatz and the lamed with a segol.

A witness…against the children of Yisrael. This meaning of our verse is tied to For when I shall have brought them (v. 20). It is also possible that our verse is independent, because Scripture states, ve-anetah (that…shall testify) (v. 21). Ve-anetah (that…shall testify) is similar to ta’aneh (bear) in thou shalt not bear…against thy neighbor (Shemot 20: 13). The song, as it were, will testify before those who ask, “Why did all this happen to us?”
Before them. Le-fanav means before them. It means that the witness will not be removed from before them but shall always be with them.
For I know their imagination. For even if I did not know the future, I know what they have done until this day.
The same day. Moshe did not tarry in doing this thing. It is possible that this took place on the day he died, which was after writing the words of the Torah, for Moshe wrote the song with it.
Until they were finished. This is connected to the words.
That Moshe commanded the Leviyim. Scripture is being brief. Our verse, as it were, says, the earlier-mentioned Leviyim who are kohanim, but not all the Leviyim, for they do not touch the ark.
[That bore the ark of the convent of Hashem.] By command. There are many such instances.

It may be there for a witness against thee. Moshe speaks to all of Yisrael. The kohanim are included when he speaks to Yisrael. However, when Moshe addressed the Reuveni and the Gadi he spoke to them alone, as I previously explained.

And how much more after my death. In addition, I know that after my death… for Hashem told me, and this people will rise up, and go astray (v. 16) after you sleep with your fathers. This is what after my death refers to.
[Befall you.] The meaning of ve-karata (and…will befall you) is similar to ve-chatat (but the fault is) in but the fault is in thine people (Shemot 5:15). It is explained there.
Give ear. I have previously explained in my book that the word ha’azinu (give ear) is related to the word ozen (ear). Scripture, as it were, says incline your ear.

I have previously informed you that the Gaon says that the meaning of heavens is the angels and the meaning of the earth is the people of the earth. On the other hand, its meaning might be that the rain that comes down from heaven and the fruit which the earth produces are called to bear witness. I believe that the correct interpretation is that Moshe called heaven and earth to witness because they last forever. Similarly Hear, O ye mountains (Michah 6:2) and also Yehoshua’s stone. Scripture there writes that the stone heard. I have hinted to you that man’s soul is intermediary between the upper and lower worlds. The soul compares all things to its body. It certainly does so when speaking to other human beings. It therefore elevates the low and lowers the high.
Shall drop. The word ya’arof (shall drop) is related to the word ya’arof (he will break down) in He will break down their altars (Hoshea 10:2). The meaning of ya’arof (shall drop) is will come down.
My doctrine. Likchi (My doctrine) refers to that which one will take away from him. It means a lesson. Compare, lekech (doctrine) in For I give you a good doctrine (Mishlei 4:2).
As the small rain. I believe that se’irim (small rain) refers to light rain.

And as the showers. The word revivim (showers) is related to the word rav (numerous). They are adjectives. The fact that esev (herb) is stronger than deshe (tender grass) is proof of this. Some say that se’irim (small rain) is related to sa’ar (hair). Others say that it is related to the word sa’arat (storm of) in storm of Hashem (Yirmiyahu 30:23) even though se’irim is spelled with a sin. Similarly, the phrase ve-yista’er alav (shall come against him like a whirlwind) (Daniel 11:40), which is spelled with a sin, means the same as ve-yista’er alav spelled with a samekh. It is also possible that the word se’irim has no brother in Scripture. Our verse repeats itself for emphasis, as is the style in all prophecies. The essence of our verse is that Moshe prayed that his words be like dew and rain which, as it is written, do not return unfulfilled but water the earth. The meaning of the latter is that Moshe’s words should enter the hearts of those who hear them in the same way that the rain affects the earth and fructifies it and causes it to produce plants.

Ascribe ye greatness. This is addressed to the heavens and the earth, as Scripture states, The heavens declare the glory of God (Tehillim 19:2), which is to be understood in accordance with my interpretation. Similarly Let the heavens and earth praise Him (Tehillim 69:35).
[The rock, his work is perfect.] Moshe opens with this phrase to make it known that all that befell Yisrael did so because of their evil deeds.

The meaning of The Rock is that Hashem, like a rock, is everlasting. Do not be amazed at this, for Scripture similarly states, Hashem…shall roar like a lion (Hoshea 11:10). Scripture does this because one who speaks cannot compare Hashem’s work to anything but His works, for everything is His work. Rock, in But Hashem is the rock of my heart (Tehillim 73:26), similarly means a support, might, and permanence. Others say that tzur (rock) is related to the word tzurah (image). Compare, tzuram (their form) in And their form shall be for the nether-world (Tehillim 49:15). Its basic meaning is that Hashem does not consist of matter, which can be molded into a form. On the contrary, He is Primary form. The first interpretation appears correct to me.

His work is perfect. All the works of an artisan are incomplete because the artisan needs the assistance of one greater than he. The work of Hashem alone is perfect. Everything is a duality except for the creator of all.

For all his ways are justice. His ways do not change. On the contrary, they follow one law. This is the praise of Hashem. All those who are created change their deeds in accordance with their needs. Hashem’s works were done for His glory, with might and wisdom. The standing still of the sun (Yehoshua 10:12) is no argument to the contrary because, as I explained in its place, its secret is clear, from the clause And thou, Moon in the valley of Ayalon (Ibid.).

A God of faithfulness and without iniquity. God alone has true might, for all the might of the mighty is an “accident;” that is, it depends on outside sources. The meaning of our clause is, it is not possible that God does iniquity because He is a God of faithfulness. It is possible that ve-en avel (and without iniquity) means and without iniquity in His ways. On the other hand, it is possible that the word El (God) is to be read as if written twice.

Just and right is he. Since Scripture states shichet lo (is corruption His) (v. 5), it says a perverse people corrupted God’s righteousness. Look, God alone is right. The rightness of the right is to fix that which is crooked. The word lo (v. 5) therefore refers to what He had at first.

No; his children’s is the blemish. Lo banav (no, his children’s) means those who say that they are not his children. Scripture similarly states, Children in whom is no faithfulness (v. 20). Its meaning is that they do not admit that Hashem created them. Although they might profess their belief verbally, they do not believe it in their hearts. The fact that they do not fear Hashem is proof of their lack of belief. The lamed of lo (his) serves itself and another word along with it. It is to be prefixed to the word mumam (the blemish). The meaning of lemumam is, because of their blemish, their blemish consisting in being A generation crooked and perverse.

And perverse. The meaning of u-fetaltol (and perverse) is he grows strong and triumphant in his crookedness. Compare the word naftule (wrestlings) in with mighty wrestlings (Bereshit 30:8). Some say that the meaning of shichet lo (is corruption His) is, they corrupted themselves; that is, they corrupted their souls. Do not wonder that the singular lo is employed, for this is the style of the language. Can you not see that Scripture reads, Remember (zekhor) the days of old, Consider (binu) the years of many generations (v. 7). I believe that shichet lo (is corruption His) means they corrupted Elokim; that is, they corrupted the ways of Elokim, which are implanted in man’s mind, as well as the statutes which He commanded. Scripture, as it were, says the crooked generation that is not His children corrupted Him. This is their blemish. The verse that follows, namely, Do you thus requite Hashem, is proof that this is its interpretation. I have explained the meaning of the heh in the book entitled Moznayim.
Foolish. In their deeds.
And unwise. In heart. Look, the entire people are totally deficient in thought and deed.
Thy father. Scripture states this because it earlier stated that they are not His children.
That hath gotten thee. Kanekha (gotten thee) is similar to kanani (made me) in Hashem made me (Mishlei 8:22).
He…made thee. Fully developed you.
And established thee. For full development.
The days of. Yemot (days of) and yeme (days of) are two forms. The same is the case with shenot (years of) and shene (years of).
Of old. Olam (of old) means the time that has past.
Ask thy father. Scripture states this because it earlier said Remember. If you forgot what your fathers told you, ask them.

And he will declare unto thee. Ve-yaggedekha means and he will declare unto thee. Compare, netattani (thou hast given to me) in for that thou hast given to me in the Southland (Yehoshua 15:19). And yetzauni (are gone forth of me) in My children are gone forth of me (Yirmiyahu 10:20).
Thine elders. Scripture repeats itself, for it is elegant to do so.

When the Most High gave to the nations their inheritance. The commentaries say that the reference is to “the generation of the dispersion” when all the earth became inhabited. Hashem at that time decreed that the land of the seven nations should belong to Yisrael, as this land would be large enough for them. Scripture therefore reads, According to the number of the children of Yisrael.

He set. Some say that yatzev (he set) is an infinitive. Compare the word dabber (speak) in behold, I cannot speak (Yirmiyahu 1:6). Others say that yatzev (he set) is a verb in the imperfect, employed as a perfect. It is like the word ya’asu (they made) in They made a calf in Chorev (Tehillim 106:19). I believe that Ask thy father alludes to those “who understand.” The same applies to “thy elders.” The meaning of the portion of Hashem is His people is similar to which Hashem thy Elokim hath allotted (Devarim 4:19), for every portion below has a portion above.

According to the number of the children of Yisrael. The rabbis, of blessed memory, say that the image of our father Yaakov is engraved on the throne of glory. The latter is a great secret. For the portion of Hashem is His people is proof of this. This is a very great status. Hashem did not do this for any nation. Scripture therefore states, Do ye thus requite Hashem, O foolish people and unwise? (v. 6), that is, a people who have fallen from their status in their foolishness. Now, this Hashem is your father, for he created you for His glory, and as Scripture goes on to explain, he taught you as a father teaches his son.
The lot. Chevel (lot) means a section. Compare, chavalim (the lines) (Tehillim 16:6). A section is so called because land is measured with a cord.
He found him. The reference is to thy father that hath gotten thee (v. 6).

The meaning of He found him is that God’s glory entered into the desert with them. Furthermore, they were like a person wandering in the wilderness, a place where no man passes, for so Scripture states. The wilderness is a waste.
A howling. A place where animals such as jackals and ostriches howl, and whoever hears their voices is astonished.
He compassed him about. The reference is to the clouds.
He cared for him. By giving him the Torah.
He kept him. From the enemies.
As the apple of his eye. I have previously explained the meaning of ishon (apple).
Scripture speaks as humans do when it says His eye. It means that God protected them from all enemies and all that lay in wait.
As an eagle that stirreth up her nest. Ya’ir (stirreth up) is a transitive verb. It means He leads them from place to place.

Her young. Gozalav means her young. The word gozal (a young pigeon) in and a turtle-dove, and a young pigeon (Bereshit 15:9) is similar. The word gozal, along with the term efrochim (young birds), is a general term. It is similar to the term tzippor (bird).
Hovereth. When they journey. Yerachef (hovereth) is related to the word merachefet (hovered) (Bereshit 1:2). The cloud acted similarly when Yisrael journeyed.

Spreadeth abroad her wings, taketh them. As an eagle takes each and every chick and bears it on her wing, for the chick does not have the strength to fly. This is the meaning of our verse. However, the meaning of how I bore you on eagles’ wings (Shemot 19:4) is connected to and brought you unto Myself (Ibid.). It means that Yisrael went out with a high hand and came quickly to Mount Sinai. It is similar in meaning to Who are these that fly as a cloud (Is. 60:8).

Hashem alone did lead them. Adonai badad (Hashem alone) means only Hashem. Its meaning is similar to At the commandment of the Hashem they encamped, and at the commandment of Hashem they journeyed (Bamidbar 9:23). Hashem had no associate. It is possible that the word badad (alone) refers to Yisrael. Compare, Lo, it is a people that shall dwell alone (Bamidbar 23:9).
And there was no strange God with him. With Yisrael. They roused Him to jealousy with strange gods (v. 16) is proof that this interpretation is correct.
He made him ride on the high places of the earth. The land of Kenaan, which is in the center of the inhabited world. He made him ride is metaphorical.

The reading of the word bamote (high places) does not change because of the vav. It is related to the word bamotemo (their high places) (Devarim 33:29). The word bemotav (with…his tomb) in the wicked…with…his tomb (Is. 53:9) is not related to our word.
Fruitage. The word tenuvot (fruitage) means fruit. It is related to the word yanuv (increase) in If riches increase (Tehillim 62:11).

Field. Sadai (field) is an adjective. It follows the paradigm of chakham (wise). The yod of sadai is in place of a heh. It is similar to the vav of shalev (at ease) in I was at ease (Iyov 16:12). The clause ya’aloz sadai (let the field exult) (Tehillim 96:12) wherein ya’aloz is in the singular proves this.

And he made him to suck honey out of the crag. This is a metaphor. It is like That the mountains shall drop down sweet wine (Yoel 4:18). The reference is to the abundance of honey and oil which, as is clearly stated in Scripture, were exported from the land of Kenaan

Out of the flinty rock. The lamed in chalmish (flinty) has no dagesh because the word is in the construct. Me-chalmish tzur (out of the flinty rock) is the reverse of mi-tzur ha-challamish (out of the rock of flint) (Devarim 8:15). The same is true of charvot tzurim (knives of flint) and tzur charbo (his sword of flint) (Tehillim 89:44).
Curd of kine. An abundance of meat.

And milk of sheep, with fat of lambs. Were it not for tradition then this verse would serve to support my opinion regarding the fat which I mentioned in its place. On the other hand, fat in with fat of lambs means the fleshy and the good. Compare, All the best (chelev) of the oil (Bamidbar 18:12).
Of the breed of Bashan. Who were raised in the mountain of the Bashan.
With the kidney-fat of wheat. This is metaphorical, for the fat lies on the kidneys. The kernel of wheat also looks like a kidney.

And of the blood of the grape. The wine. The Land of Yisrael thus contains an abundance of honey, oil, meat, bread, wine, and all sorts of fruit. This is the meaning of the fruitage of the field (v. 13). Some say that honey refers to date honey.
Foaming wine. The word chamer (foaming wine) means wine. Compare, kerem chemed (a vineyard of foaming wine) (Is. 27:2).

[Thou drankest foaming wine.] The tav of the word tishteh (thou drinkest) is a second person prefix. Our verse, as it were, speaks like a person who tells his friend the land has so much wine that you will drink it at all times. Some say that enav (grape) is in the feminine. However, what they say is worthless, for the tav should have been vocalized with a pattach so that it would be a causative. Some say that tishteh speaks of the community, for the word Yisrael is sometimes in the masculine and sometimes in the feminine. This interpretation is a bit closer to the correct meaning.

But Yeshurun waxed fat. Yeshurun refers to Yisrael. It is possible that the name Yeshurun is related to the word yashar (upright). Its meaning is, the one who was upright became fat. Some say that the word Yeshurun is related to the word ashurennu (I behold him) (Bamidbar 23:9). The first interpretation appears “upright” in my eyes. The fact that Yeshurun is in the singular is proof of this.
And kicked. The word va-yivat (and kicked) is similar to tivatu (kick ye) in Wherefore kick ye (Shmuel I 2:29). Its meaning is to be ascertained from its context.
Thou didst wax fat. It did not enter their minds to take stock of themselves.
Thou didst grow thick. The word avita (thou didst grow thick) is similar to the word avah (thicker) in My little finger is thicker (Melachim I 12:10).

Thou didst become gross. Some say that kasita (thou didst grow thick) is similar to kissah (he hath covered) in he hath covered his face with his fatness (Iyov 15:27), for the word is found in the kal conjugation. Others say that kasita is similar to ke-seh (like…a sheep) in I have gone astray like a lost sheep (Tehillim 119:176). We do not find such a construction in any of the verbs. It appears to me the word kasita has no brother. Its meaning is, you kicked.
And he forsook. The commandments of his Elokim.

And contemned. In mind and verbally. Its correct meaning is that Yisrael profaned the name of Hashem for not saving him. He caused this to be. Scripture therefore continues, the Rock of his salvation, which is to be understood as The Rock, His work is perfect (v. 4).
They roused him. In their thoughts. Compare, and now nothing will he withheld from them (Bereshit 11:6).
With strange gods. Be-zarim is to be interpreted as with strange gods.
With abominations. The reference is to idols.

Demons. Shedim (demons) has the same meaning as se’irim (satyrs) in the satyrs after whom they go astray (Vayikra 17:7). Therefore Rabbi Yitzchak the son of Shaul who rests in Eden says that the word se’arum (dreaded) in Which your fathers dreaded not is related to the word se’irim. The lamed of la-shedim (unto demons) pertains to shedim and also to another word. La-shedim lo eloha (unto demons, no-gods) is to be read as if written la-shedim u-le-lo eloha (unto demons and unto no-gods). I believe that there is no need for this interpretation. On the contrary, the meaning of la-shedim lo eloha is clearly, unto demons who are no-gods. They are called shedim in the same way that the Eimim are called Eimim. They are called shedim because they destroy reason.

Gods that they knew not. How could Yisrael think that these gods were deities when they did not know these gods by proof. This is the meaning of they knew not. Neither did they know them by tradition. This is what Which your fathers dreaded not refers to.
New gods that came up of late. A few days ago. They are not ancient. Even their fathers did not know them.

Dreaded. Se’arum means they were not in dread of them. Se’arum is related to the word ve-yista’er (shall come like a whirlwind) in shall come against him like a whirlwind (Daniel 11:40). It is similar in meaning to sa’ar in That made the hair (sa’arat) of my flesh to stand up (Iyov 4:15). However, it appears that se’arum is related to the word sa’arah (storm) even though the latter is spelled with a samekh. Se’arum is similar to yetza’uni (are gone forth of me) in My children are gone forth of me (Yirmiyahu 10:20) and in chazaktani (Thou hast overcome me) in Thou hast overcome me, and hast prevailed (Yirmiyahu 20:7); that is, you are more powerful than me. Look, the meaning of se’arum is, they were not afraid of them.

Of the rock that begot thee thou wast unmindful. These are the words of the prophet. He wonders: How did you forget the One who begot you? You served new gods. Also, this clause, the rock that begot thee, is similar to Look unto the rock whence ye were hewn (Is. 51:1). Yisrael, as it were, came from Hashem, for everything comes from Hashem’s might. Compare, That spread the earth by Myself (Is. 44:24). One must be amazed by those who err in their hearts because Scripture states, This day have I begotten thee (Tehillim 2:7). They have forgotten this verse.

[Thou wast unmindful.] The word teshi (thou wast unmindful) is related to the word tinnasheh (you will forget) in [the clause] you shall not forget. The missing silent letter following the tav is in place of the omitted dagesh which compensates for the first root letter, and the yod is in place of the heh. Compare the word temchi (blot out) in Neither blot out their sin (Yirmiyahu 18:23). Both words are accented penultimately in order to show a difference between the masculine and the feminine in verbs whose last letter is a silent heh. However, it appears to me that the yod is superfluous. It follows the same rule as tet (decline) does in neither decline (Mishlei 4:5).

That bore thee. Mecholelekha means that bore thee. Observe, God who is powerful and mighty as a rock [gave birth to you]. It is possible that the word mecholelekha is related to the word chil (pain), as in Like as a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery, Is in pain (tachil) (Is. 26:17).
And spurned. Scripture similarly writes, veyanetz ha-shaked (And the almond-tree shall blossom) (Kohelet 12:5). On the other hand, it might be an intransitive verb.
His sons and his daughters. Men and women, for they too sacrificed to the idols.
And he said. Hashem in His heart or to the angels.
I will hide my face. Scripture speaks as people do. Similarly I will hide Mine eyes from you (Is. 1:15). It means that when they search for Me they will not find help.

I will see what their end will be. Some say that our verse is to be interpreted, I will hide My face from them because I see what they will ultimately do. However, it is to be understood according to its literal meaning, that is, [so that] I will see what they will do when trouble comes upon them.
For they are a very froward generation. This is connected to I will hide My face.

Froward. They turned about and served gods besides Me. They were My children, for I gave birth to them. Look, there is no faithfulness in them. The word emun (faithfulness) is a noun. On the other hand, it might be an adjective meaning there is no faithful man among them, for we find for the faithful fail (Tehillim 12:2) in which faithful is parallel to godly (Ibid.). We also find that keepeth faithfulness (emunim) (Is. 26:2).
They have roused me. The second root letter has no dagesh in order to simplify enunciation.
With a no-God. Its meaning is, a god that has no power to deliver.
With their vanities. Rather than with something which truly exists.
I will rouse them. Akni’em (I will rouse them) is a hifil. It describes two actions.

With a no-people. A nation who are not My people. Scripture describes how God shall anger them. He will bring upon Yisrael, upon Yisrael alone, unique troubles which surpass the adversity that he brought upon all others.
A vile nation. For a fool and a vile person lack understanding. He therefore kills and has no pity.

Kindled. Their provocation, or that which they did, for we find the word kadechah (kindled) to be transitive, as in For ye have kindled (kedachtem) a fire in My nostril (Yirmiyahu 17:4). It is possible that kadechah means is kindled. It is like the word chaveru (came as allies) (Bereshit 14:3), the meaning of which is gathered. All of this refers to God’s burning anger.
Unto the depths of the nether-world. Its meaning is similar to that of and that the whole land thereof is brimstone, and salt, and a burning (Devarim 29:22).
And devoureth. Yisrael.
And setteth ablaze. Va-telahet (and setteth ablaze) is related to the word lahat (flaming) in and the flaming sword (Bereshit 3:24).
The mountains. The mountains of Yisrael.

I will heap. Some say that the word aspeh (I will heap) means I will add. However, it really means I will consume. Compare, tispeh (sweep away) in Wilt Thou indeed sweep away (Bereshit 18:23). The aforementioned is so, even though aspeh and tispeh differ in conjugation. It means that there will be no evil that will not come upon them. Scripture compares the evils to arrows that suddenly appear and there is no way to guard oneself against them.
The wasting of hunger. Meze ra’av (the wasting of hunger) means burnt by hunger. Meze (wasting) is similar to le-meze (that they should heat) in that they should heat the furnace (Daniel 3:19).

And the devouring of the fiery bolt. Le-chume reshef (the devouring of the fiery bolt) means consumed by birds. Compare, As the birds (bene reshef) fly upward (Iyov 5:7). It appears to me that Scripture mentions the four evil punishments. They are: starvation, which is what The wasting of hunger refers to; and the devouring of the fiery bolt, And bitter destruction refers to the plague; And the teeth of beasts will I send upon them refers to the beast: and finally [there is] the sword, as in Without shall the sword bereave (v. 25). Reshef (the fiery bolt) is thus similar to reshfeha rishpe esh (The flashes thereof are flashes of fire) (Cant. 8:6). It means that the air will grow hot.
And …destruction. Ketev means destruction.

Bitter. Meriri (bitter) refers to bitterness in the air. Compare, ke-meriri yom (like the bitterness of the day) (Iyov 3:5). Scripture similarly writes, Nor of the destruction (ketev) that wasteth at noonday (Tehillim 91:6). The latter refers to the plague. The word u-lechume in u-lechume reshef (and the devouring of the fiery bolt) means devoured by. There are many such instances.
With the venom of crawling things of the dust. The reference is to being bitten. Venom refers to being bitten.

[Dust.] This refers to fiery snakes. Zochale (crawling) is related to the word fear. They are called zochale because all who see them are afraid of them. It is similar to the term emim. This is so because there are adjectives [without nouns]. Its counterpart is found in the speech of Elihu the son of Barachel (Iyov 32:6).
Both young man. This is connected to Without shall the sword bereave. Scripture reads gam (both)
The word also is out of place here. in accordance with the rules of the Hebrew language, as I have previously explained. Look, the Torah includes all: young men, virgins, old men, and youths.

I would make an end of them. Some say that the word afehem (I would make an end of them) is a combination of three words. Actually, it has no neighbor. Its meaning is, I will destroy them, for Scripture states afterwards, I would make their memory cease from among men. Look, all of them will die. If the grammarians who say that afehem means I will scatter them to all the corners are right, then the idea expressed by the first part of the verse is not to be connected to that of the second. Some say that the meaning of afehem is, I will destroy them in my anger. Behold, the meaning of afehem is, I will destroy them. Afehem is similar in meaning to ashbitah (I would make…cease). Scripture repeats itself. This interpretation would be correct were it not for the alef of afehem, for the word should have read anfehem, meaning I will be angry at them. The first interpretation is correct.
[I thought.] The meaning of amarti (I thought) is, I said to Myself. The Torah speaks as people do.

I dreaded. Agur means I dreaded. It is related to the word va-yagar (was sore afraid) in And Moav was sore afraid (Bamidbar 22:3). The Aramaic translation connects it to the word agerah (gathereth) in And gatherest…in the harvest (Mishlei 6:8). Actually it is related to the word tigrah (fight). Scripture speaks as people do so that those who hear will understand.

Should misdeem. Yenakkeru (misdeem) is the reverse of yakkiru (they shall recognize). Yenakkeru is similar to va-yitnakker (but made himself strange) in but made himself strange unto them (Bereshit 42:7).
Hath wrought all this. Upon the tribes.

For they are a nation void of counsel. The reference is to the enemies of Yisrael. This is its correct interpretation. The word ovad (void) is an adjective. It is in the construct. It is therefore vocalized with a pattach beneath the bet. It is known that the word ovad is an intransitive verb. The correct interpretation of ovad etzot is that etzot (counsel) reverts to ovad (void). It is similar to novelet aleha (whose leaf fadeth) (Is. 1:30). The same is true of ve-tovedu derekh (and ye perish in the way) (Tehillim 2:12) wherein tovedu is connected to derekh. The Aramaic translator who rendered ovad etzot as me’abbede etzah (void of counsel) understood this.

If they were wise. If they were wise and understood that Hashem did all of this to Yisrael because of all their sins, they would comprehend their eventual end, namely, that Hashem would do so because of their sins.

How should one chase. If Yisrael was wise they would understand how one of their enemies could pursue a thousand Bnei Yisrael. This occurred only because their Rock has forsaken them. Others interpret our verse as how did Yisrael, who are now weak, at first pursue a thousand of their enemies.

Except their rock had given them over. Mekharam means had given them over. The same applies to yimkor (will give over) in for Hashem will give Sisera over (Jud. 4:9). Its meaning is that Hashem, as it were, gave them over as in payment for their deeds. It is thus a literal sale.

Had delivered them up. Hisgiram (had delivered them up) is similar to yisgor (shutteth up) in, He shutteth up a man (Iyov 12:14). On the other hand, it might be similar to hasgiro (deliver him up) in and our part shall be to deliver him up (Shmuel I 23:20).

For their rock is not as our rock. These are the words of Moshe. Moshe explains for they are a nation void of counsel (v. 28). It means that our Rock has handed us over, and the nations have no rock like our Rock, and they are no better than we are. Scripture similarly states, and our enemies are not judges. Compare, And I have not learned wisdom (Mishlei 30:3). Others say that the meaning of Even our enemies themselves being judges is as follows: our enemies admit this. It is therefore not connected to For their vine is of the vine of Sedom (v. 32).
And of the fields of Amorah. Scripture repeats itself. The same is true of Their clusters are bitter.
The venom of. Look, the wine is like the venom of angry serpents.

And the cruel poison of asps. Petanim (asps) is similar to the word paten (asp) in on the hole of the asp (Is. 11:8). Even though rosh (poison) is spelled with an alef, it has the same meaning as its counterparts which are spelled with a vav.
Cruel. Akhzar (cruel) means mighty. The alef is superfluous, like the alef of etzba (finger) and ezro’a (arm).

Is not this laid up in store with me. These are the words of Hashem. Some say the reference is to the decrees. It appears to me that the reference is to their wine, which is the poison of asps. It is laid in store until they drink it. The meaning of the word kamus (laid up in store) is to be ascertained from its context, for it has no family.
Sealed up in my treasuries. So that no hand touches it. It is kept for them, for vengeance is to be exacted from them.

Vengeance is mine, and recompense. Shilem (recompense) is a noun. It is like the word kitter (offering) in The offering…did not (Yirmiyahu 44:21). It means that Vengeance is mine, and mine is the recompense to compensate them in accordance with their deeds.
Against the time when their foot shall slip. It means they will fall and be unable to stand.
The meaning of Against the time is similar to that of Yea, even the wicked for the day of evil (Mishlei 16:4). It is a great secret.
For the day of their calamity is at hand. Let them not think that the vengeance will be exacted from their children.

And the things that are to come upon them shall make haste. Ve-chash atidot lamo (and the things that are to come upon them shall make haste) means each one of the future events that are to come upon them shall make haste. It is like Its branches (banot) run (tza’adah) over the wall (Bereshit 49:22). Or the meaning of ve-chash atidot lamo is, the day (yom) when the future things that are to come upon them makes haste. The first interpretation is correct. The word chash (make haste) comes from a root in which only two letters are present.
The meaning of the things that are to come is, the evil things that are about to come.
For Hashem will judge his people. Elokim will exact judgment from Yisrael’s enemies on behalf of His people. It is like Be Thou my judge, O Elokim, and plead my cause (Tehillim 43:1).
And repent himself. I have previously explained this.

Their stay is gone. The stay of Yisrael. Yad (stay) means the strength. The tav of azelat is in place of a heh, for both the heh and the tav are signs of the feminine. The word ve-shavat (then it shall return) in then it shall return to the prince is similar (Yechezkel 46:17).
And there is none remaining, shut up or left at large. When the captives are numerous, the captors take some of them and leave others, but in this case almost all are lost.
And it is said. And the enemy shall say.
The rock in whom they trusted. This is to be understood in accordance with my previous interpretation.

Who did eat. Scripture employs the language of the enemies who thought that the burnt offerings serve as food for Elokim. Scripture employs the plural as they do. The Torah therefore states, I, only I, am He, And there is no god with Me (v. 39).

The wine of their drink-offering. Yen nesikham (the wine of their drink-offering) is similar to venisko yayin (and the drink-offering thereof shall be of wine) (Vayikra 23:13). They are two terms. Some say that yen nesikham (the wine of their drink-offering) means the wine of their king, for the kings used to donate the wine for the burnt offering. Compare, nesikhe midian (the princes of Midyan) (Yehoshua 13:21). The first interpretation appears correct to me.
And help you. Ve-yazrukhem (and help you) is similar to berakhnukhem (we bless you) (Tehillim 119:26). If you say that the Lord alone is God then let Him protect you from the coming troubles.

I, even I. The word I is written twice. Compare, I, even I (Is. 51:12). On the other hand, its meaning might be, I am He, and I do not change. The latter is the correct interpretation, for Elokim has no co-worker. I am He that put Yisrael to death, and I will bring them back to life. Look, they were not saved. There is none that can deliver you out of My hand, even you out of My hand, until I execute My judgment upon you. Many say that we can derive the existence of life in the future world from this verse. They offer proof from the fact that Scripture first states, I kill and then, I make alive. It similarly reads, Hashem killeth, and maketh alive (Shmuel I 2:6). He bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up (Ibid.) is proof. Others offer proof from: And surely your blood of your lives (nafshotekhem) will I require (Bereshit 9:5). Also from And it shall be righteousness unto us (Devarim 6:25); for that is thy life (Devarim 30:20) in the world to come, and the length of thy days (Ibid.) in this world; that it may go well with thee (Devarim 5:16). Rabbi Hai Gaon, of blessed memory, says that Scripture had no need to state clearly that a future world exists because it was known by tradition. I believe that [Scripture does not speak of a future world] because the Torah was given to all. It was not given to an individual alone. The topic of the world to come is not comprehended by even one in a thousand, for it is very abstruse. The reward in the world to come is contingent on the nature of the soul. The reward is given for the service of the heart. The latter consists in comprehending the works of Elokim, for they are the ladder whereon one ascends to the level of understanding the knowledge of Elokim, which is what is most important. Observe, the Torah itself explains to the intelligent the topic of the tree of life. Behold, there is a power by which one can overcome the cherubim. The one who eats from the tree of life gains eternal life like the ministering angels. The psalm of the sons of Korach similarly reads, Hear this, all ye peoples…(Tehillim 49:2). The secret is But Elokim will redeem my soul from the power of the nether-world; For He shall receive (take) me. Selah (Tehillim 49:16). Scripture similarly states, And afterward receive (take) me with glory (Tehillim 73:24). Both verses employ the word “taking” as Scripture does in the account of Chanoch and Eliyahu. Now, since Scripture states, But Elokim will redeem my soul [from the power of the netherworld] (Tehillim 49:16), how could it say, For too costly is the redemption of their soul (Tehillim 49:9)? The intelligent will understand.

For I lift up my hand to heaven. An oath taken over something which is everlasting. For I lift is similar to when he lifted up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven and swore by Him that liveth for ever (Daniel 12:7). The term I lift up is an anthropomorphism so those who hear will understand.
As I live for ever. As I live so will I do this.

If I whet. Shannoti (I whet) comes from a double root. Compare, channoti (I am loathsome) in And I am loathsome to the children of my tribe (Iyov 19:17). Shannoti is related to the word shanun (sharp) in and a sharp arrow (Mishlei 25:18).
And my hand take hold on judgment. The sword is the instrument by which the warrior executes judgment.
I will render vengeance to mine adversaries. The meaning of ashiv (I will render) is, I will do to Mine adversaries as they did to Yisrael. This is also the meaning of And will recompense (ashallem).
With the blood of the slain. This explains I will make Mine arrows drunk.
[The captives.] It means the wounded.
From the…heads. This explains shall devour flesh. It means that the head shall be chopped off.
Long-haired. The word parot (long-haired) is similar to bi-fero’a pera’ot (When men let grow their hair) (Jud. 5:2). The rabbis also employ the term ha-nifra (one who collects).

Sing aloud, o ye nations. Then, when Hashem avenges Yisrael’s blood, the nations will praise Him. Some say that the meaning of harninu (sing aloud) is similar to the word rinnah (cry) in And there went a cry (Melachim I 22:36). It means the herald. Proclaim about them in every place where they are.

And doth make expiation for the land of his people. Some say that a vav is missing. Our verse should be interpreted as if written ve-khipper admato ve-ammo (and doth make expiation for His land and for His people). According to the midrash the meaning of ve-khipper admato ammo (and doth make expiation for His land of His people) is that the land makes expiation for His people. This interpretation is true in itself. However, it is not the meaning of the verse. Furthermore, the word adamah (land) is a feminine. The heh at its end is proof of this. The tav takes the place of the heh. Now, Scripture does not read vekhipperah (and doth make expiation). In my opinion the meaning of our clause is that the people will make expiation for the land, for we find Scripture stating, avanim shachaku mayim (The waters wear the stones) (Iyov 14:19). The word kippur (expiate) is also found without the word al (for), as in ve-khippartahu (and make atonement for it) in, thus shalt thou purify it and make atonement for it (Yechezkel 43:20). The meaning of ve-khipper admato ammo is that Yisrael will execute vengeance upon the nations and they will make atonement for the Land of Yisrael because of the blood that was shed in it. Compare, and no expiation can be made for the land [for the blood that is shed therein, but by the blood of him that shed it] (Bamidbar 35:33). This interpretation is in keeping with the meaning of the context. On the other hand, the meaning of ve-khipper (and doth make expiation) is, and will purify, as in ve-khippartahu (and make atonement for it) (Yechezkel 43:20). Yechezkel similarly said, regarding the end of the wars, Thus shall they cleanse the land (Yechezkel 39:16). Yisrael will thus purify the land.

And Moshe came. Our verse teaches that after Moshe went to each one of the tribes and charged them, when he came to the tent of meeting and all of the children of Yisrael were gathered unto him, he spoke the words of this song.

He, and Hoshea the son of nun. This is similar to Then sang Moshe and the children of Yisrael (Shemot 15:1). Also, this was done to exalt the status of Yehoshua in the eyes of all. Scripture refers to Yehoshua by the name of Hoshea because it was the name by which he was known to all of Yisrael, for who aside from the elect of the assembly knew that Moshe referred to Hoshea by the name of Yehoshua. The approach of the midrash is known.
Because it is your life. Its meaning is similar to that of The fear of Hashem prolongeth days (Mishlei 10:27). Furthermore, you shall be in a good land and not in exile.
That selfsame day. The day that he delivered the song.

And die. To prepare himself for death, for Moshe, as I will explain, was to bury himself. I have hinted earlier what one of the wise men of the generation said regarding the word va-ye’asef (and was gathered) (Bereshit 25:8).
Because ye sanctified me not. I have previously explained this.
The land. This explains thither.
And this is the blessing. This blessing is similar to the blessing of Yaakov.
The man of Elokim. This teaches that Moshe blessed them prophetically.
Before his death. Close to his death. This means on the day of his death.

Came from Sinai. The Gaon, of blessed memory, says that Mount Sinai, Seir, and Paran are close to each other. This verse speaks of the revelation at Sinai. Scripture reads mi-sinai (from Sinai), for mi-sinai has the same meaning as be-sinai (on Sinai). The same applies to the term mise’ir (from Seir).
From the myriads holy. The reference is to the angels. Scripture speaks of the Divine presence, which descended.

A fiery law unto them. The Torah, which was given through fire and lightning. He says that the Hashem came…is a prayer. It means, You who came to Sinai and bequeathed the Torah, Let Reuven live (v. 6). However, this interpretation is far-fetched, for Scripture should read, keep Reuven alive and do not put him to death. Those who lack faith say that from Seir refers to the religion of the Edomim, and Paran refers to the faith of the Yishmeelim. However, these err. Do they not see that Moshe commenced at first to bless Yisrael alone. Scripture thus reads, wherewith Moshe the man of Elokim blessed the children of Yisrael (v. 1). Scripture goes on to say ve-zarach mi-se’ir lamo, the meaning of which is, And rose from Seir unto them. Compare, lamo (for them) in And there is no stumbling for them (Tehillim 119:165). It appears to me that this chapter is a general blessing to all of Yisrael. Moshe then goes on to address each tribe and tribe individually. Then Moshe includes them all in the verse which reads, There is none unto Elokim, O Yeshurun (v. 26). Look, we find that Devorah said, Hashem, when Thou didst go forth out of Seir, When Thou didst march out of the field of Edom, The earth trembled (Jud. 5:4). Clearly the field of Edom is not a mountain as the Gaon says, for the Gaon maintains that Sinai, Seir, and Paran are three mountains close to each other or facing each other. Also, the Book of Tehillim states, O Elokim, when Thou wentest forth before thy people, When Thou didst march through the wilderness (yeshimon); Selah (Tehillim 68:8). Scripture then states, The earth trembled (Tehillim 68:9). Now the Divine presence did not march through the wilderness (yeshimon) on the day that the Torah was given, for Yisrael came to the wilderness (yeshimon) after they had passed through the wilderness (midbar) of Paran. Furthermore, Chavakuk says, Elokim cometh from Teiman (Chavakuk 3:3). Teiman was one of the sons of Edom, for we read, Teiman, Omar (Bereshit 36:11). From Teiman means the same as from the field of Edom. Look, all the verses speak of war. Let Elokim arise, let His enemies be scattered (Tehillim 68:2) is proof of this. Scripture describes Elokim’s saving of His servants in terms of help coming down from heaven, the earth melting, the mountains dissolving, and the heavens quaking. Then the earth did shake and quake (Tehillim 18:8) in David’s song is proof of this. I have explained the meaning of even yon Sinai (Tehillim 68:9) in its place. The following is the explanation of our verse. Hashem came refers to the glory that entered into Yisrael. It first entered Yisrael at Sinai. And rose from Seir means that Elokim did not show His might among the nations all the years that Yisrael was in the wilderness until Yisrael came to the field of Edom. Scripture similarly states, in their mount Seir, unto Eil Paran (Bereshit 14:6). Seir and Paran are thus close to each other. The meaning of And rose from Se’ir is thus explained, for mi-seir means from the place of Seir; that is, when Yisrael came to Seir, Elokim’s glory rose to Yisrael. He shined forth from mount Paran repeats the idea expressed by and rose from Seir. It means that Elokim here showed His shining.

And he came from the myriads holy. I believe that this is connected to At His right hand. It means that fire came from the myriads holy at Hashem’s right hand to surround Yisrael. It is similar to the horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha (Melachim II 6:17).
[Fiery law.] The meaning of law is something constant.
