Yea, he loveth the peoples. Hovev (loveth) comes from an Aramaic word. It has the meaning of then ye shall be Mine own treasure from among all peoples (Shemot 19:5). The peoples refers to Yisrael. Compare, After thee, Binyamin, among thy peoples (Jud. 5:14); They shall call peoples unto the mountain (v. 19).
[All his holy ones.] This refers to the sons of Levi.
They are in thy hand. They are round about the ark.
And they sit down at thy feet. This means they will walk in Your ways. The meaning of in Thy hand is, you will protect them.
Receiving of thy words. They will teach Torah. They are the ones who transmit the oral Torah.
Receiving. Each and every one. This is so even though they are many.
The meaning of Thy words is, that which You spoke they will bear, for they are the bearers of the Torah, and they also carry the ark.
The word yissa (receiving) is similar to tissa (uttering) in Thou shalt not utter a false report (Shemot 23:1).

And they sit down. Tukku (sit down) has no brother. Some say that it is related to the word mi-tokh (from the midst of). They, as it were, walk in the midst of Your feet. Others say that the tav is in place of a heh. It is like the tav of tirgalti (I taught) in I taught Efraim (Hoshea 11:3). The meaning of our verse is, even if they are beaten on Your account, they will not forsake Your words. However, this is farfetched. Actually it means are drawn; they go to the place of the ark which serves as the footstool for Hashem’s feet. This is the blessing: May Hashem be a wall of fire round about Yisrael. May Yisrael be Hashem’s treasure. May the Leviyim always teach the Torah.

Moshe commanded us a law. This is what they shall bear upon their lips and say from generation to generation: thus did we copy with our hands an inheritance from the mouth of Moshe. The lamed of lanu (us) applies to itself and also to another word. Morashah kehillat ya’akov (an inheritance congregation of Yaakov) should be read as if written morashah le-kehillat ya’akov (an inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov). It is similar to ve-hanevu’ah oded ha-navi (even the prophecy Oded the prophet) (Divrei Hayamim II 15:8). Or morashah (an inheritance) should be read as if written twice. Our clause should be read as if written an inheritance, an inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov.

A king. The reference is to Moshe, from whose mouth the heads of the people clearly heard the words of the Torah. The meaning of our verse is that Moshe was the equivalent of a king, and the heads of the tribes were gathered unto him. This interpretation is supported by Scripture’s statement that the Torah was given to the kohanim, who, in my opinion, are meant by All His holy ones-they are in Thy hand (v. 3), and to all the elders of Yisrael (Devarim 31:9). This is what When the heads of the people were gathered refers to. Scripture also writes there, Assemble unto me all the elders of your tribes (Devarim 31:28). Rabbi Yehudah Ha-Levi, of blessed memory, says that the king alludes to the Torah. He similarly used to explain there was no king in Yisrael (Jud. 18:l).

Let Reuven live. Moshe starts with the first-born, for this is the proper practice. He does not mention Shimon because of the incident of Ba'al Peor, for those who served Baalpeor were from the tribe of Shimon. Their number proves this. Also, their prince was killed. It is also possible that Moshe followed in the footsteps of Yaakov, who did not bless Shimon and Levi. The tribe of Levi was blessed out of respect for Aharon. Shimon had no one as great as Aharon. Should one who disputes argue, “Why did Moshe bless Reuven?” The answer is that Yaakov blessed Reuven. The blessing was have not thou the excellency (Bereshit 49:4). The meaning of the latter is that Reuven shall be like one of his brothers. Moshe mentions Yehudah after Reuven because he was in charge of a standard and he was the first to lead in battle. Next Levi and then Binyamin are mentioned because the Leviyim dwelled in Yerushalayim, which was situated between Yehudah and Binyamin. Scripture clearly states this. Moshe then mentions the tribe of Yosef so as not to delay naming him. He had already mentioned his younger brother. He next mentioned Zevulun because he waged war. He then mentioned Yissachar. After Moshe finished mentioning the children of the wives, he commenced with Gad, who camped among the standard of the children of the wives. Moshe then mentions Dan, who was in charge of a standard. He then mentioned Naftali because he was older than Asher.
Let Reuven live. A prayer.
And not die. For it is possible that he will be as a person who lives a certain number of years and then dies.

In that his men become few. Ve-yehi metav mispar is to be rendered, and let his men not be numbered (few). It is similar to And I have not learned wisdom (Mishlei 30:3) and to the bet of be-el shaddai (as God Almighty) (Shemot 6:3) as I have explained many times. Moshe said this because it is possible for the tribe of Reuven to live forever but consist of few people. All things that are numbered are few. Compare, And I am men of number(Gen. 34:30).

And this for Yehudah. He similarly said to Yehudah, “Let Yehudah live and not die.” He also added, “Hear, Hashem, the voice of Yehudah” when he goes to war, because Yehudah would go into battle first.
And bring him in unto his people. To the camp, which was in Gilgal. On the other hand, it might be a prayer regarding those who go to do battle in the land of the enemy.

His hand shall contend for him. Rav lo (contend for him) means shall be sufficient for him so that he has no need for anyone to help him but Hashem’s help alone. Others say that the word rav is related to the word merivah (conflict). The meaning of yadav rav lo is that his hands shall fight for him. Others say that the word rav is like the word rav (shot forth) in and He shot forth lightnings (Tehillim 18:15). It is related to va-robbu (and shot at him) (Bereshit 49:23).
And of Levi. U-le-levi amar (and of Levi he said) is to be interpreted, And of Levi he said to God. Compare, say of me (li): He is my brother (Bereshit 20:13).
With thy Holy One. Le-ish chasidekha (with Thy holy one) means to the man who is Your holy one.

Whom thou didst prove at Massah. Massah is a noun. It means a test. The meaning of our clause is: Aharon was pious. Aside from the incident at Merivah, for which You already punished him, no unseemly thing was found in him. Also, this verse supports my interpretation regarding the incident of the calf, that is, that Aharon made the calf for Hashem’s glory.
[Thy Tumim and thy Urim.] This means may Thy Tumim and Thy Urim always be his and his seed’s.
Who said. Moshe speaks of the tribe. Shmuel who came to the house of Hashem as soon as he was weaned, to be trained in Hashem’s service, is an example.
Nor knew he his own children. There were among them individuals who begot children for the service of Hashem. FOR THEY HAVE OBSERVED

Thy word, and keep thy covenant. Compare, They kept (shameru) His testimonies, and the statue that He gave them (Tehillim 99:7) so that they would teach them to Yisrael. Some say that the reference is to Whoso is on Hashem’s side, let him come unto me (Shemot 32:26).
They shall put incense. The reference is to those among them who are kohanim.
And whole burnt-offering. Kalil (whole burnt offering) refers to the olah (burnt offering).
Bless, Hashem, his substance. The first-born and the tithe.
The work of his hands. The sacrifices.
Smite through the loins. Smite them that rise against him.
That they rise not again. Min yekumun (that they rise not again) means of those that will rise against them. Compare, la-yam mekhassim (cover the sea) (Is. 11:9).
Of Binyamin he said. Le-vinyamin means of Binyamin. Moshe said of Binyamin, who is the beloved of Hashem, Binyamin shall dwell in safety by Hashem, and Hashem shall dwell between his shoulders.
He covereth him. The reference is to God’s glory which, as Scripture writes, dwelled in Binyamin’s portion, in Yerushalayim.

The meaning of between his shoulders is, in the center of his inheritance. Or between his shoulders means that God’s glory was visible. Furthermore, between his shoulders is also connected to covereth.
For the precious things. Which the heavens will give.
The fruits of the sun. For the fruits of the seed and the vineyard are dependent upon the sun.

The yield. Geresh (yield) is related to the word vayigreshu (cast up) in And its waters cast up (Is. 57:20). The moon does this via the moisture which is in the air, for its heat is unlike the power of the sun. Scripture reads moons because they renew themselves, and there are many of them in the year.
And for the tops. This means and for the precious things that grow on the tops of the ancient hills.
The everlasting hills. Scripture repeats itself.
And for the precious things of the earth. Scripture repeats itself. The earth refers to flat land.
And the fulness thereof. From what it is full of.
And the good will of him that dwelt in the bush. The reference is to heaven.

Let the blessing come. Tavotah (let the blessing come) refers to this blessing. Two signs, the tav and the heh, are joined together. Compare, ezratah (help) (Tehillim 44:27); yeshu’atah (salvation) (Tehillim 3:3); ba-tzaratah (in…distress) (Tehillim 120:1). Moshe compared the tribe of Yosef to a bullock because he earlier spoke of produce. Moshe referred to Yosef as His firstling bullock (v. 17) because a first-born bullock has great strength as it is the first of its father’s might.
Majesty is his. His body is large. It means that the tribe of Yosef is large in number.
The horns of the wild-ox. In power.
The ten thousands of Efraim. As in the words of Yaakov.
Rejoice, Zevulun, in thy going out. To war. Similarly Zevulun is a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death (Jud. 5:18).
In thy tents. Compare, For he saw a resting-place that it was good (Bereshit 49:15).

They shall call peoples unto the mountain. Zevulun shall possess great wealth because he dwells where ships dock. This is the meaning of they shall suck the abundance of the seas. The word shefa (abundance) is related to the word shifat (caravan) in The caravan of camels shall cover thee (Is. 60:6).

And the hidden treasures of the sand. The word sefune (hidden) has no brother. It has the same meaning as temune (treasures). Similarly admat afar (dust). The meaning of the hidden treasures of the sand is that Zevulun will have so much wealth that they [the tribe] will hide it in the sand. And because of their wealth, they will come in a multitude to the mountain of Hashem to offer sacrifices of thanksgiving to Hashem.
Enlargeth Gad. Moshe compares Gad to a lion. All who see him will flee from him. No one shall torment him.
And he chose a first part for himself. This means he looked out for himself and sought an inheritance before the other Bnei Yisrael.
For there a portion of a ruler was reserved. The word chelkat (portion of) means a portion.
[A ruler.] Mechokek (ruler) refers to someone who is great and a ruler. Compare, My heart is toward the governors (le-chokeke) of Yisrael (Jud. 5:9).

[Reserved.] The word safun (reserved) is similar to safun (ceiled) in and it is ceiled with cedar (Yirmiyahu 22:14); and sefunim (ceiled) in be-vattekhem sefunim (Chaggai 1:4), which means your houses which are ceiled. The import of ki sham chelkak mechokek safun (for there a portion of a ruler was preserved) is that Gad saw the paneled palaces that were the portion of the nobles of the Emori.
Came. Va-yeta (came) is missing an alef. The meaning of our clause is that the heads of Gad came armed with the children of Yisrael. Moshe prophetically saw this.

He executed the righteousness of Hashem. Gad fulfilled with his hands that which he spoke with his mouth, for the children of Gad vowed that they would go out with Yisrael to wage battle against their enemies. Moshe did not mention Reuven. It is possible that he omitted Reuven because the tribe of Gad were greater warriors than the tribe of Reuven. The words of Chronicles, which states regarding the tribe of Gad, whose faces were like the faces of lions (Divrei Hayamim I 12:9), is proof of this. We do not find this stated regarding the tribe of Reuven.
Leapeth. The word yezannek (leapeth) has no companion in Scripture. Our clause is to be understood as follows: Moshe compared Dan’s might to that of a lion’s whelp leaping from Mount Bashan.
Satisfied with favor. Seva ratzon (satisfied) is an adjective. It means he will be sated with favor.
The sea and south. Yam ve-darom (the sea and south) means that Naftali’s inheritance shall be in the southwest.
The favored. Ratzuy (favored) means the beloved.
And let him dip his foot in oil. Because of the abundance of oil. It is similar to He washeth his garments in wine (Bereshit 49:11). Yaakov similarly said, his bread shall be fat (Bereshit 49:20).
Iron and brass shall be thy bars. For mountains of iron and brass shall be in his portion.

And as thy days, so shall thy strength be. The word dovekha (thy strength) has no neighbor. The interpretation of the Aramaic translation is known, namely, that you will be strong all your days. Some say that the alef of dovekha is in place of the doubled letter. It is like the word baze’u (divide) in Whose land the rivers divide (Is. 18:2). They believe that dovekha is related to the word dovev (moving gently) in Moving gently the lips of those that are asleep (Cant. 7:10). This interpretation is not reasonable.
There is none like unto God, o Yeshurun. Moshe goes back to bless all of Yisrael.
Who rideth upon the heaven. That is, who is mighty. The fact that He rideth upon the heaven is proof of this.
[And in his excellency on the skies.] It means, the heavens stand by God’s might.

The eternal Elokim is a dwelling-place. Note that the word ma’on (dwelling-place) means a covering (i.e., a sukkah). In Shalem also is set His covering (sukko), And His dwelling-place (me’onato) in Tziyon (Tehillim 76:3) is proof of this. There are many such examples. The meaning of our verse is: The eternal Elokim is your covering. Compare, Even the Most High, thy habitation (me’onekha) (Tehillim 91:9) and Thou hast been our dwelling-place (ma’on) (Tehillim 90:1). The ma’on (dwelling place) is always above the one who takes refuge in it. The “place” is below.
And underneath are the everlasting arms. Which will support you.

Scripture reads everlasting to teach that it shall always be so. The hand will not weaken, and your covering (ma’on) will not be removed, for He is the eternal God. The meaning of kedem (everlasting) is that God has no beginning and no end. Scripture speaks in human terms when it speaks of beginning and end. The Gaon says that and underneath means and underneath God. He did not explain anything.
The fountain of Yaakov. All those who came forth out of the fountain of Yaakov. Similarly And are come forth out of the fountain of Yehudah (Is. 48:1).
In a land. El eretz is to be rendered, in a land. It is similar to if they pray in this place (el ha-makom ha-zeh) (Melachim I 8:35).

Yea, his heavens. The heavens of the earth or of Yisrael. The meaning of our verse is, it is the nature of the land to produce corn and oil. Also, the heavens shall always give their dew and there will be no need to water the ground.
Who is like unto thee. Among the nations.
The shield of thy help. No evil shall come upon you.
And that is the sword. He is the sword by which you will exalt yourself over all your enemies.
Shalt tread. Tidrokh (shall tread) is similar to midrakh (to tread on) in for the sole of the foot to tread on (Devarim 2:5). The contents of our verse are similar to the account of Gidon.

And Moshe went up. I believe that Yehoshua wrote from this verse onward, for Moshe did not write after he ascended. Yehoshua wrote prophetically. And Hashem showed him; And Hashem said unto him (v. 4); and also, And he was buried (v. 6) are proof.
So Moshe the servant of Hashem died there. Even in his death Moshe, like a servant, did what Hashem commanded him.

According to the word of Hashem. For Hashem told him, Get thee up (Devarim 32:49) and die (Devarim 32:50). Scripture similarly writes with regard to the death of Aharon, at the commandment of Hashem (Bamidbar 33:38). It similarly states, At the commandment of Hashem they encamped (Bamidbar 9:23).

And he was buried. Moshe buried himself. He entered a cave in the valley. The same is true of but the shepherds fed them (otam), and fed not My sheep (Yechezkel 34:8) and, And the officers of the children of Yisrael did see them (otam) (Shemot 5:19). Note, Mount Avarim is also known as Mount Nevo. Nevo is in the image of Mercury. Mount Avarim is also known as “the valley which is the top of Pisgah which is over against Beit Peor.” The fact that Scripture tells us that Yisrael journeyed from Bamot to the valley that is in the field of Moav, by the top of Pisgah (Bamidbar 21:20) is proof of this. Furthermore, Scripture writes, And Moshe went up from the plains of Moav unto mount Nevo, to the top of Pisgah (v. 1). Moshe died there and his grave is there. Scripture states, So we abode in the valley over against Beit Peor (Devarim 3:29). Now, Scripture tells us that after Yisrael dwelt in the valley…the children of Yisrael journeyed, and pitched in the plains of Moav (Bamidbar 22:1). Another verse states, And [Yisrael] pitched in the mountains of Avarim, in front of Nevo. And they journeyed from the mountains of Avarim, and pitched in the plains of Moav (Bamidbar 33:47,48). Look, it is clear that Moshe’s burial place was in the place where he died.
Unto this day. These are the words of Yehoshua. He probably wrote this at the end of his days.

His natural force. The heh of lechoh (his natural force) is in place of a vav. It is like the heh of oholoh (his tent) (Bereshit 9:21). Lechoh is related to the word lach (moist, fresh). Scripture notes this because old people are overtaken by dryness.
The word nas (abated) is the reverse of diffused.
The children of Yisrael. However, when Aharon died, even all the house of Yisrael (Bamidbar 20:29) mourned out of respect for Moshe.
So…were ended. When the days of weeping in the mourning of Moshe were ended there, the children of Yisrael hearkened unto Yehoshua.

Was full of the spirit of wisdom. The reference is to the spirit of Hashem. For Moshe had laid his hands upon him is proof of this, for there was not found in Yisrael one such as Yehoshua for Moshe to lean on.
And did as Hashem commanded Moshe. That they hearken unto Yehoshua.
Face to face. I have previously explained this.
The mighty hand. The wonders at the sea.
The great terror. When Yisrael stood before Mount Sinai.
